sources.entry: Higgs - Dashboard and chat app for the Higgs inference server: runs MLX models on Apple Silicon behind OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs, routes to remote providers, and traces every request.

summary.one_liner: Higgs is a Rust-based local LLM inference server for Apple Silicon, built on MLX, that exposes OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs, routes to remote providers, and ships a desktop console showing per-request performance.
summary.what_it_does: Serves open-weight MLX models from Hugging Face IDs or local paths on a Mac, with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/models) and an Anthropic-compatible one (/v1/messages, /v1/messages/count_tokens). It proxies requests to providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Ollama behind the same URL, translating between wire formats, with regex routes, aliases, a default provider, and an optional auto-router. Metrics are exposed at /metrics and /v1/system, including time to first token, decode tokens per second, and prefix-cache hits. A CLI provides serve, start/stop daemon, a terminal attach dashboard, init, doctor, shellenv, and exec commands to point tools like Claude Code or Aider at the server. A desktop app (ui) offers a dashboard, model and provider views, a chat with a per-request trace waterfall, and a config editor.
use_cases: run local LLMs on a Mac with Apple Silicon
point Claude Code, Aider or other OpenAI clients at a local model
route requests to local and remote providers through one endpoint
measure time to first token and tokens per second for local inference
serve Hugging Face MLX checkpoints behind an API
inspect and replay chat requests with a performance trace
notable: Translates between OpenAI and Anthropic wire formats so existing clients work unchanged
Desktop chat includes a request trace waterfall covering prefill, cache hits, generation and tool calls, with Replay and Copy as curl
Benchmarks in the README compare decode throughput and memory against mlx_lm, vllm-mlx, llama.cpp and Ollama on an M4 Max
Supports prefix caching, continuous batching for transformer families, and quantized KV cache
Metrics and dashboard endpoints do not count toward traffic statistics
caveats: Apple Silicon only; built on MLX and requires a Mac
Source builds need Rust 1.88+, Xcode Command Line Tools and mlx.metallib next to the executable
Desktop app .dmg is unsigned and needs right-click Open on first launch
Only MLX checkpoints are supported; unknown model families are rejected
keywords: chat with local model on mac
